g.text: Fresh generation through complete retained output
Diamonds: medians. Open marks: all trials. Lines: observed min–max, not confidence intervals. Lower is better.
NumPy uses FP64; native CPU/Metal and WebGL use FP32. NumPy/WebGL use four 25M batches; native uses full buffers. No precision-neutral speedup
Readback: WebGL streams 1.600 GB RGBA without retaining the complete output; Metal copies and retains 1.200 GB XYZ. Both clocks include the draw.
Fresh pipelines generate inputs and retain complete output: NumPy 2.400 GB XYZ; WebGL 1.600 GB RGBA. New buffers; startup/setup and validation
WebGL includes input-preparation UI yields. Its M4/M5 readback gap remains unexplained; desktop runs do not establish a hardware ranking.
Full 300M-XYZ checks: every native trial; final WebGL readback and NumPy resident output; every fresh pipeline. No angular-order or physics
Lorium swap used: CPU 8,863.25M → 9,426.25M; native 9,811.62M → 13,393.06M. Memory pressure was present; hosts were not exclusive.
M5 native outputs passed, but contemporaneous compile log/binary hash were not supplied. Its executable provenance is weaker than M4.
